system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Rust (reading the book)
G2: Go (did the tour)
G3: machine learning (unfinished course)
G4: AWS certification (course only, no exam)
G5: Terraform authoring
G6: official team lead title

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Copying the 'Learning: Rust, Go' line as skills
T2: Turning the unfinished AWS Cloud Practitioner course into a certification or the unfinished ML course into ML skills
T3: Calling him Tech Lead / Team Lead as a job title (project tech lead only; acting lead only in notes)
T4: Claiming Terraform authoring
T5: Failing to condense: keeping duplicated Älvgrind sections, hobbies, gymnasium, band
T6: Dropping qualifiers like 'Vue (a little)', 'Tailwind (some)'
T7: Old cover letter is to his current employer and says he is at Sjöbris

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Oskar
Full-Stack Engineer | React, TypeScript, Node.js
Professional Summary
Full-stack developer with professional web development experience since 2014, strongest in frontend
development. Builds onboarding features with React, TypeScript, NestJS and PostgreSQL, with
experience in AWS integrations, A/B testing and technical leadership. Delivered an identity
verification flow associated with an increase in onboarding conversion from 61% to 74%.
Technical Skills
- Frontend: React, TypeScript, React Native, Angular.
- Backend and databases: Node.js, NestJS, Express, PostgreSQL, Prisma, TypeORM.
- AWS: ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS; application development and integrations.
- Integrations: Swedish BankID provider SDK, S3 presigned URLs, Firebase Cloud Messaging.
- GraphQL: maintenance of one backend-for-frontend (BFF) using Apollo Server.
Professional Experience
Fullstack Developer | Älvgrind Fintech AB | 2021-Present
- Develop onboarding features using React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL and AWS.
- Built a Swedish BankID identity verification step supporting QR-code and same-device flows
through a provider SDK. The flow was A/B tested on 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding
conversion increased from 61% to 74%.
- Implemented document uploads of up to 20 MB using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV virus scanning
in Lambda, and scan-status processing through SQS into PostgreSQL.
- Worked on the incremental migration of the onboarding backend from Express to NestJS, route by
route behind the same API gateway, using TypeORM and later Prisma. Presented the migration at
a meetup in 2022.
- Served as acting team lead for four months in 2024 during the team lead’s parental leave,
conducting one-to-ones and sprint planning.
Developer | Sjöbris Digital Agency AB | 2018-2021
- Developed client web and mobile projects using Angular, React, React Native, Node.js, Laravel and
WordPress.
- Led the technical delivery of a React Native ferry ticket app in a two-developer team, building
most of the app while the other developer handled the payment backend. The app supports ticket
purchases and offline ticket display and reached approximately 50,000 downloads.
- Used TypeScript and Firebase Cloud Messaging on the ferry app project, delivered in 2019-2020.
Newspaper website development | Nordkust Media | 2014-2018
- Developed newspaper websites over four years before joining Sjöbris Digital.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Oskar
Application: Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) - Patient Experience
Dear Verdane Care hiring team,
Your Patient Experience role closely matches the work I do at Älvgrind Fintech: building
user-facing onboarding features with React and TypeScript, supported by NestJS APIs and
PostgreSQL. Frontend development is my strongest area, alongside hands-on backend
experience. That combination is directly relevant to building Verdane Care’s booking and
intake journeys end to end, where straightforward interactions matter to the people using
them.
One example is the Swedish BankID identity verification step I built in 2022, supporting both
QR-code and same-device flows through a provider SDK. It was A/B tested on 10% of traffic
before full rollout, and onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%. This experience
connects well with your focus on simplifying patient journeys: delivering the interface and its
supporting services, then evaluating the effect on completion.
I have also implemented document uploads using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in
Lambda and scan-status processing through SQS into PostgreSQL. Alongside this, I worked
on an incremental Express-to-NestJS migration behind the existing API gateway. These
projects provide relevant experience for third-party integrations and document-handling
features, without equating fintech identity documents with the specific privacy requirements of
health data.
My experience also includes technical leadership of a React Native ferry ticket app with
approximately 50,000 downloads, and four months as acting team lead in 2024, including
one-to-ones and sprint planning. I would bring that delivery experience, a strong React and
TypeScript foundation, and practical NestJS and AWS experience to your small squad. I
would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my work on onboarding and document flows
could contribute to Verdane Care’s patient experience.
Kind regards,
Oskar

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
